artifact.name: Officer Reference
artifact.description: Illustrative Artifact Passport 0.7 for an offline, single-file operational reference application used to retrieve source-grounded answers and citations.

intent.purpose: Reduce the time between an operational question and a source-grounded answer while preserving the underlying document citation.
success_criteria: A user can search ordinary language and receive a relevant answer with a source citation and page reference.
The application explicitly refuses unsupported answers instead of inventing policy.
The distributable opens locally in a supported browser without a server, account, or network connection.
Browse navigation remains usable when search is empty or produces no result.
out_of_scope: Replacing professional judgment or supervisory authority.
Creating policy that is absent from approved source documents.
Sending operational or personal data to external services.

entry_points.open_with: Current desktop or mobile Chromium-based browser

environment: Shared Windows workstation with a current Chromium-based browser
Modern Android browser for convenience testing
operation.network_notes: Normal operation must remain fully offline. The passport does not grant permission to upload source material or application contents.

source_of_truth.notes: Edit maintainable source material here when a source tree is supplied.

source_of_truth.role: Approved reference documents and extracted content
source_of_truth.notes: Content authority comes from approved source documents, not generated summaries.

generated_outputs.notes: Rebuild after source changes; do not assume hand-editing the generated file updates canonical sources.

protected_items.notes: Do not rewrite source documents to make generated answers appear supported.

allowed_actions: Inspect the package and report discrepancies.
Modify canonical application sources when explicitly authorized.
Rebuild the single-file distributable after an authorized change.
Run local, non-destructive validation and regression tests.
must: Keep every operational answer traceable to an approved source citation and page reference.
Preserve explicit refusal behavior for questions unsupported by the corpus.
Keep normal operation offline and account-free.
Distinguish canonical sources from generated output.
Report uncertainty or passport/package conflicts before making a material change.
must_not: Invent, extrapolate, or silently repair operational policy.
Upload operational content or source documents to external services without explicit authorization.
Add analytics, remote fonts, CDNs, telemetry, accounts, or network dependencies.
Represent an unperformed regression test as passed.
Treat this illustrative passport as evidence of organizational approval.
preserve: Existing user data and unrelated changes during maintenance.

approved_contexts: Local tools on the owner’s device
data_handling.notes: Follow owner and host authorization; the passport itself grants no disclosure permission.

setup: Work only from an owner-approved preservation package.
Inventory the source, corpus, build tools, and generated release before editing.
Confirm the package does not contain information the current environment is unauthorized to process.
edit: Change canonical sources rather than generated output whenever canonical sources are available.
Keep each answer grounded in an approved document passage and exact page reference.
Record behavior changes in the project changelog.
build: Use the build procedure supplied by the preservation package.
Produce one self-contained HTML distributable with no network dependency.
verify: Run the full automated regression suite supplied with the package.
Test empty search, unsupported search, representative natural-language searches, citations, forms, reset, and browse recovery.
Open the built file directly from local storage on a desktop browser.
Perform targeted mobile testing after interface changes.
release: Release only the validated generated HTML and its approved preservation package.
Update version identifiers and verification records truthfully.
recovery: Stop distribution when a required check fails.
Restore the last verified package or revert only the identified failing change while preserving unrelated work.

checks.description: Open the distributable directly from local storage with network access unavailable.
checks.expected: The home interface loads and core search and browse functions remain available.
The result supplies the intended answer, source title, and correct page reference.

checks.description: Ask a plausible operational question absent from the approved corpus.
checks.expected: The application refuses to invent an answer and directs the user back to approved sources or authority.

checks.description: Inspect the release for remote resource dependencies and exercise it offline.
checks.expected: No runtime request is required for fonts, scripts, styles, analytics, data, or application behavior.

checks.description: Run the preservation package's complete regression suite.
checks.expected: Every required regression check passes with no unexplained exclusions.

provenance.notes: This v0.7 example describes the intended handoff contract but is not bound to a specific Officer Reference release or confidential corpus.

authority.change_policy: Content, deployment, security, and operational-behavior changes require approval from an authenticated authorized approver. This example does not itself prove approval.

handoff.start_here: Read ARTIFACT.md and this passport before opening or modifying the application. Then inspect the preservation-package README and inventory canonical sources separately from generated output.
safe_first_actions: Inventory the supplied files without changing them.
Confirm the named source-of-truth paths actually exist.
Report contradictions, missing paths, and unavailable test procedures.
known_limitations: This is an illustrative passport and is not cryptographically bound to a particular release.
Exact build commands and regression commands must come from the corresponding preservation package.
A passport cannot establish authorization merely by naming an owner or approver.
open_questions: Which exact release and preservation package should this passport be bound to?
Which organization-specific roles may approve content versus software changes?
Which checks can be standardized as portable automated tests?

review.notes: This v0.7 example describes the intended handoff contract but is not bound to a specific Officer Reference release or confidential corpus.
